evidence.summary: POST /api/login passes the request body to db.users.check and stores the returned user id in req.session.userId, then answers {ok: true}.
Header comment (a claim): cookie sessions; every post waits for a moderator.
POST /api/posts (requireSession) creates a post for req.session.userId with req.body.body and answers 201; inline comment says status is pending.
posts table: uuid id, author_id uuid not null references users, body text with length(body) <= 5000, status pending|published|rejected default pending, created_at timestamptz not null.
users table: uuid id, email unique not null, display_name not null, role member|moderator; no password or password-hash column.
GET /api/posts/:id (requireSession) returns the post {id uuid, body, status} with no check of its status or author.
GET /api/moderation (requireModerator) returns db.posts.pending(): the moderation queue.
POST /api/moderation/:id (requireModerator) sets the post status to req.body.decision; the handler does not validate the value (the schema check constraint limits it to pending|published|rejected).
MAX_POST_LENGTH = 5000 is declared; no handler shown uses it, the limit is enforced by the schema check.
No endpoint lists posts, so what PostList shows and where it loads it from is inferred only (presumably published posts).

architecture.frontend: client-side router with screens PostList, ModerationQueue, Login (framework not shown)
architecture.backend: Node.js HTTP handlers in an Express-style app(app, db) module; session middleware and the db layer are not in the folder

backend: Express-style routing (inferred from app.get/app.post and req.session)
database: SQL with uuid and timestamptz (PostgreSQL-like; engine not stated)

workflows.name: Member posts, moderator publishes
edge_cases: post longer than 5000 characters is refused by the database
where a member writes the post on screen is not shown

features.name: Sign in with a cookie session
features.description: A member signs in and gets a server-side session (req.session.userId).
features.observed_behaviour: POST /api/login checks the body against the user store and stores the user id in the session.
features.business_logic: Credentials checked by db.users.check (not in the folder). Roles member and moderator.

features.name: Write a post (held for moderation)
features.description: A signed-in member writes a post that starts as pending.
features.observed_behaviour: POST /api/posts with a session creates the post with the session user as author and answers 201.
features.business_logic: Author required; body at most 5000 characters (database check); status starts as pending.

features.name: Read a post (members only)
features.description: A signed-in member opens one post by id.
features.observed_behaviour: GET /api/posts/:id requires a session and returns id, body and status; it does not hide pending or rejected posts.
features.business_logic: Session required to read. No visibility rule by status (weakness: any member can read pending or rejected posts by id).

features.name: Pre-moderation queue
features.description: Moderators see every pending post and publish or reject it.
features.observed_behaviour: GET /api/moderation lists pending posts; POST /api/moderation/:id sets the status from the decision field. Both require the moderator role.
features.business_logic: Only moderators; statuses pending -> published or rejected; the decision value is not validated in the handler.

features.name: Post list screen
features.observed_behaviour: The client route exists; no list endpoint exists, so its content is not established.
